title: API 570 Training in Chicago: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep for Chicago piping inspectors: Whiting and Joliet unit piping, CUI in freeze-thaw winters, CMLs and injection points, self-paced online.
h1: API 570 training in Chicago: exam preparation for process piping inspectors, from the Lake Michigan shore to the Illinois River plants
html:
API 570 exam prep for Chicago process piping inspectors

On a refinery plot plan the vessels are the landmarks, but the piping is most of the inventory. A large Chicago-area refinery carries many miles of unit and interconnecting pipe, much of it insulated, some of it running hot heavy crude and some of it carrying light hydrocarbons that would flash on release. API 570 is the in-service code for that piping, and the API 570 Piping Inspector certification is the credential owner-users and contractors around Chicago ask for when someone has to own circuits, set CMLs and sign off thickness surveys.

Atlantis NDT's API 570 course prepares you for the examination. It is self-paced and online, with an instructor who answers your questions as you study. There is no Atlantis classroom in Chicago: you work from home, from a contractor's trailer or from a hotel near the next job. The American Petroleum Institute decides eligibility, administers the exam in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification.

Where the pipe runs around Chicago

Four big sites and a ring of terminals hold most of the region's in-service process piping.

  • bp's Whiting refinery in north-west Indiana, about 440,000 barrels a day, has three crude units. Oil & Gas Journal reported that the largest, at 250,000 barrels a day, was reconfigured in 2013 alongside a new 102,000 barrel-a-day coker and a 105,000 barrel-a-day gas oil hydrotreater, so that heavy, sour crude could make up most of the feed. Its products include jet fuel for the Chicago and Detroit airports.
  • ExxonMobil's Joliet refinery in Will County runs twelve major process units and moves gasoline and diesel by pipeline to Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, with asphalt and coke leaving by truck, barge and rail. Manifolds, a barge loading dock and rail loading add transfer piping to the unit piping.
  • A refinery at Lemont, listed in EIA's 2026 capacity report with delayed coking and catalytic cracking, adds another full set of hot and overhead systems.
  • LyondellBasell's Morris plant makes ethylene, propylene and polyethylene, which means compressor piping, light hydrocarbon lines and cold-section systems quite unlike a refinery's.

Terminals bring a different kind of piping work. Kinder Morgan's Argo terminal on the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal has three barge docks, receives product from the West Shore pipeline and injects into the Sanders line that carries jet fuel to Midway Airport. Its Chicago terminal on the Calumet River and Lake Calumet handles chemicals, ethanol, biodiesel, caustics, acids and vegetable oils, each with its own materials and transfer lines. A piping inspector who moves between a refinery and a terminal meets very different services in the same week.

Corrosion under insulation through a freeze-thaw winter

CUI is the mechanism a Chicago piping inspector lives with. Carbon steel is most at risk between about 10°F and 350°F, and much insulated plant pipe either runs in that band or cycles through it, sometimes several times a winter. The local climate adds its own wetting routes:

  • steam tracing that leaks under the insulation, often unnoticed until the jacket stains;
  • jacketing seams that open as metal and cladding expand and contract through freezes and thaws;
  • snow and meltwater lying on horizontal runs, pipe supports and insulation penetrations;
  • lines shut down for a turnaround, cooled into the CUI range and left wet before restart.

For the exam, CUI is RP 571 paragraph 3.22, one of fifteen mechanisms the current API 570 Body of Knowledge selects. Its neighbour 3.17, chloride stress corrosion cracking, matters on austenitic stainless lines where wet insulation concentrates chlorides on the outside of the pipe. Learn where CUI concentrates, which inspection techniques find it with the insulation on or off, and how API 570 expects susceptible systems to be identified and inspected. The CUI detection guide walks through the field methods.

Damage on heavy-crude units, and what it does to a CML programme

When a refinery switches to heavier, more sour crude, the piping inspector feels it first, because circuits that once thinned slowly can start to move. The mechanisms below are the ones a Chicago candidate meets on the job that also sit in the current API 570 selection from RP 571.

Where on a Chicago-area unitMechanism to study (RP 571)What it means for CMLs
Hot crude, vacuum and coker transfer linesSulfidation (3.61)Attack can vary fitting to fitting, because carbon steel components with low silicon content can thin faster than the pipe either side, so a few readings per circuit are not enough.
Crude tower overhead and condensing systemsHydrochloric acid corrosion (3.37), sour water corrosion (3.58)Damage concentrates where water first condenses, so CMLs go at the dew point region and downstream of wash water injection.
Downstream of control valves, at elbows and reducersErosion and erosion-corrosion (3.27)Readings cluster on the outer radius and immediately downstream of the turbulence.
Small-bore connections near pumps and compressorsMechanical fatigue, including vibration (3.43)A visual and vibration check, rather than thickness, is what finds it.
Amine and caustic systemsAmine stress corrosion cracking (3.3), caustic corrosion and cracking (3.14, 3.15)Cracking near welds that were not stress relieved needs crack detection methods, not thickness gauging.

A CML programme on units like these is never finished. Each turnaround's readings feed corrosion rates, rates feed intervals, and a crude slate change can make last year's circuit boundaries wrong. Expect exam questions that test the logic of circuits: grouping piping of similar material, temperature and service, and treating injection points and dead legs as places that need their own attention.

Injection points and dead legs on Chicago units

Setting out an injection point circuit

API 570 gives recommended limits for the circuit around an injection point. Upstream, it starts at least 12 in. or three pipe diameters before the injection point, whichever is greater. Downstream, it ends at the second change in flow direction past the injection point, or 25 ft beyond the first change in flow direction, whichever is less. Take a wash water injection into an NPS 8 overhead line, outside diameter 8.625 in. Three diameters is 25.9 in., more than 12 in., so the circuit starts about 26 in. upstream. If the first elbow is 6 ft downstream and the second is 40 ft beyond that, the second change of direction is 46 ft away, but 25 ft beyond the first elbow is only 31 ft, so the circuit ends at 31 ft. Candidates who stop at the second elbow every time lose this mark.

Dead legs in a cold climate

A dead leg collects water and corrosive deposits at its low point, which is why API 570 asks inspectors to identify dead legs and inspect them deliberately rather than leave them to the circuit average. Around Chicago a stagnant branch has a second way to fail: trapped water freezes and splits the pipe. Bypasses around control valves, idle pump suction branches and drain stubs that missed winterization are the usual suspects. The practical answer is often removal or reliable draining and tracing; the examination answer is usually about where the readings go and why.

Worked example: an LPG line the owner has classed as Class 1

Classification is the owner-user's decision, based on the consequence of a leak, and the class sets the maximum interval. Suppose an NPS 6 Schedule 40 line carrying LPG, nominal wall 0.280 in., is classed as Class 1, and the required thickness given in the problem is 0.150 in.

  1. Readings at the thinnest CML: 0.262 in. nine years ago, 0.244 in. four years ago, 0.220 in. today.
  2. Long-term rate = (0.262 − 0.220) ÷ 9 = 0.0047 in. per year. Short-term rate = (0.244 − 0.220) ÷ 4 = 0.0060 in. per year. The short-term rate is higher and reflects current service, so use it unless the problem gives a reason not to.
  3. Remaining life = (0.220 − 0.150) ÷ 0.0060 = 11.7 years; half of it is 5.8 years.
  4. Class 1 caps thickness measurement at 5 years, so the next thickness inspection is due in 5 years, and the external visual interval for Class 1 is also 5 years.

Change one input and the answer moves. Had the owner classed the same line as Class 2, the thickness interval would be the half-life figure of 5.8 years, because the Class 2 cap is 10 years, while the external visual interval would stay at 5. Questions like this test whether you check every limit, not just the arithmetic. The API 570 explainer summarises the rules the example draws on.

Where the plant piping ends and the pipelines begin

Chicago sits on a crossroads of liquid pipelines, and piping inspectors here work right up to their fences. Enbridge's two long-haul crude systems on its Lakehead network terminate in Indiana, its Line 62 runs from the Griffith terminal to the Flanagan terminal near Pontiac, and its Line 78 runs from Pontiac through north-west Indiana to Sarnia. Pipeline segments like these are regulated by the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration under 49 CFR Part 195, with their own integrity rules. API 570 is written for piping inside the plant or terminal, and where an owner draws the boundary at a meter station, pig trap or block valve is set in its own procedures. The exam expects you to know API 570's scope; your employer's procedure tells you where your circuits stop.

Getting to API 570 eligibility from a Chicago job

API combines education with piping experience gained in the last ten years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency, including owner-user inspection organisations. The routes, in local terms:

  • UT thickness technicians taking readings for a CML programme are performing inspection activities. With a high school diploma API asks for three years of piping experience including one year of inspection; a two-year engineering or technology credential reduces that to two years.
  • Pipefitters and welders from turnaround and construction work can count fabrication and repair years towards the total, but still need a year in supervision or performance of inspection.
  • Operators can count operating experience with the piping, and often earn the inspection year after moving into an inspection role.
  • Engineers with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology need one year of supervising or performing inspection.

Without formal education the requirement is five or more years. The API 570 certification requirements page sets out the military service rules and how API verifies experience.

Working B31.3 into a Chicago shift pattern

Most of the open-book half comes from ASME B31.3, and most of B31.3's bulk is not examined. The current Body of Knowledge excludes, among others, paragraph 302 apart from 302.3.3 and 302.3.4, the parts of 304 beyond straight pipe under internal pressure and permanent blanks, Chapters VII, VIII and IX and a list of appendices. Welding procedure review is limited to P-No. 1, 3, 4, 5 and 8 base metals, and brazing is not covered. Knowing what you can ignore is half the battle when study time comes in two-hour pieces between night shifts.

A pattern that works for many local candidates: learn API 570's corrosion rate formulas and interval rules first, because they can appear closed-book, then its MAWP rule for corroded pipe; then practise B31.3 pressure design, leak test pressures and impact test exemptions until the paragraph numbers are familiar; then work ASME B16.5 flange ratings from the tables rather than from memory. When a question will not resolve, send it to the instructor with your working; the reply points to the clause, which is what you will need to find again under time pressure. Free API 570 practice questions give a first check of where you stand.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group from a Chicago site

Refineries, chemical plants and inspection contractors often move a whole thickness crew towards API 570 together, so the people who take readings can also own circuits. One enquiry can cover the group, fees are quoted on request, and each candidate studies at their own pace before applying to API individually. Atlantis also trains UT technicians under ASNT SNT-TC-1A and, in the United States, performs UT, MT, PT and VT inspection but not radiography; see ultrasonic pipe thickness testing for the field service.

faq.q: Can I prepare for API 570 in Chicago without travelling to a class?
faq.a: Yes. The Atlantis course is online and self-paced, so you study from home or a job site and send questions to the instructor whenever a clause or calculation stalls. There is no Atlantis classroom anywhere in the Chicago area. You travel only for the examination, which API holds in person at a Prometric test centre after accepting your application.

faq.q: Are frozen and split dead legs on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Freezing is not one of the RP 571 mechanisms selected in the current Body of Knowledge, so you will not be examined on it as a damage mechanism. Dead legs are examined through API 570 itself: why they corrode, how they should be identified and where the readings belong. In a Chicago plant the freezing risk is still very real, so treat it as job knowledge alongside the examined rules.

faq.q: Does inspecting traced and insulated lines for CUI at Whiting count as inspection experience?
faq.a: It can. Looking for and assessing corrosion under insulation, removing insulation at susceptible points and taking readings are inspection activities when you do them under the plant's piping programme, while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency. Record the circuits, techniques and findings as you go, because API verifies the experience described on your application.

faq.q: Is transfer piping at a terminal such as Argo or Lake Calumet covered by API 570?
faq.a: Terminal transfer and dock piping is often inspected under an owner's API 570-based programme, but the boundary depends on the owner's procedures and on whether a line is part of a pipeline regulated under 49 CFR Part 195. The exam tests API 570's scope as written. Experience on in-scope terminal piping can count towards eligibility if it meets API's experience rules.

faq.q: I take UT thickness readings for a contractor in the suburbs. How close am I to API 570?
faq.a: With a high school diploma, API asks for three years of piping experience, including one year spent performing or supervising inspection, gained in the last ten years with an authorized inspection agency. Thickness surveys under a CML programme are inspection activities, so many technicians are closer than they think. Check the certification page, count your documented years and start studying while you close any gap.

faq.q: Which B31.3 calculations should a Chicago candidate practise for API 570?
faq.a: Pressure design thickness of straight pipe, the minimum thickness of a permanent blank, the casting and weld joint quality factors, hydrostatic and pneumatic leak test pressures, the impact test exemption temperature and the preheat and heat treatment tables. Add API 570's corrosion rate, remaining life, interval and MAWP rules, and B16.5 flange ratings. Thermal expansion from Appendix C also appears.

faq.q: Should a Joliet piping inspector add API 510 later?
faq.a: Many do, because owner-user departments value inspectors who can cover both the vessels and the piping connected to them. The two exams share corrosion rate logic, welding inspection and Section V and Section IX, so the second is easier than the first. API 570 is usually the natural first step for someone who already spends most days on piping circuits.

faq.q: Can a contractor enrol its whole UT crew for API 570 prep?
faq.a: Yes. Send one enquiry listing the candidates and the exam windows they are aiming at, and the quote covers the group. Each technician studies at their own pace with access to the instructor, then applies to API and sits the exam individually. Because eligibility is personal, confirm each person's documented piping experience before enrolling them.
